0.long_answer: LDL receptors are categorized into different classes based on the nature of the mutations affecting their function. Specifically, Class IV defects are characterized by a failure in the internalization process because the receptor cannot properly cluster in clathrin-coated pits, which is essential for the inward budding (invagination) of the plasma membrane during receptor-mediated endocytosis. As a result, although the receptor may bind LDL normally, it is unable to be internalized into the cell, leading to decreased clearance of LDL from the bloodstream.
